detailed_description: The HTML Encoder/Decoder converts text between raw characters and HTML entities directly in your browser. Paste text into the input area, then click Encode HTML to convert characters such as `<`, `>`, `&`, `"`, and similar markup characters into entities like `<`, `>`, `&`, and `"` using the browser's built-in `textContent` to `innerHTML` conversion, or click Decode HTML to turn named and numeric entities (such as `&`, `&`, `&`) back into their original characters. The result appears in a read-only output box that you can copy with one click, and a Clear button resets both fields. The tool does not transform code into safe HTML, sanitize against XSS by itself, validate against any HTML specification, support batch file processing, or download results as files.
usage_steps: Paste or type the text you want to convert into the input textarea.
Click Encode HTML to turn raw characters into HTML entities, or Decode HTML to turn entities back into characters.
Read the result in the output textarea below the buttons.
Click Copy to put the output on your clipboard.
Click Clear when you want to reset both the input and the output.
usage_examples: Encode a snippet that contains `<div class="hero">` so it can be shown literally in a tutorial.
Decode an `&quot;` and `&#38;` mixed string to inspect what the original text looks like.
Convert a small block of HTML before pasting it into a Markdown code example.
Round-trip a string by encoding it and then decoding the result to confirm it matches the source.

faqs.question: What is the difference between encoding and decoding HTML?
faqs.answer: Encoding converts special characters (like <) to HTML entities (<). Decoding reverses this process, turning entities back into characters.

faqs.question: Does this tool handle all HTML entity references, like numeric codes?
faqs.answer: Yes, it processes both named entities (e.g., &) and numeric/decimal entities (e.g., &).

faqs.question: Will encoding affect the spaces or line breaks in my text?
faqs.answer: No, standard spaces and line breaks are preserved. Only characters with specific HTML entities are converted.

faqs.question: Is there a limit to the amount of text I can convert at once?
faqs.answer: The tool is optimized for typical web development tasks. For extremely large documents, processing in sections is recommended.

faqs.question: Is my data secure when using this online encoder/decoder?
faqs.answer: Yes, all processing happens in your browser. Your text is never sent to or stored on our servers.
